items.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data
items.summary: Microsoft is warning organizations that it suffered a data breach after attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Entra Connect Health service to gain unauthorized access to administrator email addresses and tenant configuration information. [...]

items.summary: The BADBOX malware found in a broad range of generic Android TV boxes has returned to large-scale ad-fraud operations following last year's disruptions. [...]

items.title: FBI reportedly hacked again, this time targeting nationwide police database
items.summary: FBI systems have reportedly been breached for the second time in two months, this time targeting the agency's National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which is used to share information between local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies. [...]

items.title: Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day
items.summary: A threat actor used autonomous Cairn AI agents to discover and exploit a critical MONAI Label vulnerability. The post Amazon: China-Linked Hackers' AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day appeared first on SecurityWeek .

items.title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats
items.summary: A malicious webpage could extract a Meta Muse user's private conversations and stored memories from the assistant without triggering any approval prompt, researchers have shown. The same attack could be extended to reach the credentials Muse stores for the user's connected accounts. items.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
items.summary: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-129975, affects all software that uses GPGME before version 2.3.0,

items.title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
items.summary: Suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to find a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging server, and gain root access to a university server, Amazon Threat Intelligence said this week. items.summary: Signal has announced that it will restrict screenshots by default to stop artificial intelligence (AI) agents from reading private chats on Android and iOS devices, but conceded that the protection is "incomplete." items.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
items.summary: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use "advanced cryptographic tools" to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption key and charging victims a markup for work that was never performed.

items.title: China's 'Armory Castle' Lays Siege to VMware vCenter Zero-Day
items.summary: During the last wave of major VMware vCenter security updates, a China-nexus threat group likely already had its next zero-day up its sleeve.

items.summary: The encrypted messaging app will now block those screenshots by default, following similar steps it took with Microsoft last year. The post Signal blocks Apple, Google AI screenshotting in response to ‘existential threat’ to privacy app appeared first on CyberScoop .
